surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Amadio’s late goal lifts the Senators past the Sabres
paras: Peyton Krebs struck first for the Sabres midway through the second, and that was all they would get. Shane Pinto tied it 1-1 for Ottawa midway through the third, and Michael Amadio put the Senators ahead for good with just over three minutes left.

The Senators had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Sabres 30-24. Samuel Ersson made 23 saves for the Sens, and Colten Ellis stopped 28 of 30 at the other end. The Senators improved to 10-6-1 and climbed to third in the Atlantic, while the Sabres fell to 7-5-3, seventh in the Atlantic.
